Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old female with ~3 weeks of progressive left-sided hearing reduction and persistent left facial numbness around the ear and jawline, associated with intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness; clinician advised same-day in-person neurological and ENT assessment for possible Bell's palsy vs other causes.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Decreased hearing on the left side and numbness of the left face (around the left ear and along the left jawline).
  - Symptoms present for approximately three weeks and are persistent at the time of the consult.
  - Occasional ringing in the ear (tinnitus); intermittent dizziness associated with episodes of ringing.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms started about three weeks ago and have persisted; patient reports the numbness is present “all the time” currently.
  - Patient reports some reduction in training/ability to work because of intermittent dizziness.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - None specifically identified.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No ear discharge.
  - No ear pain.
  - No fever.
  - No itching in ear reported.
  - No weakness elsewhere in the body.
  - No difficulty swallowing or speaking.
  - No visual problems.
  - No other systemic symptoms reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No documented fever, ear discharge, ear pain, dysphagia, dysarthria, visual changes, or limb weakness.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps — intermittent symptoms; uses an intranasal steroid spray as needed (prescription obtained previously; name not recalled).
- Remote history patient recalls as “labyrinthitis” (patient could not confirm details; reported as remote, not ongoing).

Medications:
- Intranasal spray for nasal polyps — name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Rennies (antacid) PRN — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other regular medications documented.

Allergies:
- Latex allergy reported.

Social History:
- Age: 40 years.
- Occupation: Jockey (horse racing); reports decreased training and workplace impact due to symptoms.
- Living situation: patient initially stated “live alone” then stated “live with my partner” — conflict noted (see Quality checks).
- Pets: none.
- Smoking, alcohol, and substance use: not documented.

Family History:
- Brother with neurofibromatosis.
- Other family history: not detailed.

Physical Examination:
- No physical exam findings documented in the transcript.
- No vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results documented.
- Plan includes in-person neurological examination and ear inspection (no results available).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left-sided decreased hearing with left facial numbness (duration ~3 weeks)
  - Assessment:
    - Clinician's provisional consideration: possible Bell’s palsy (to be confirmed by physical exam).
    - Clinician stated this is unlikely to be immediately life-threatening based on history but requires face-to-face assessment to exclude other causes.
  - Plan:
    - Same-day, face-to-face clinic appointment requested for neurological examination and otoscopic ear inspection.
    - General Practitioner/clinic to perform full neurological exam to confirm diagnosis and exclude alternative etiologies.
    - Administrative team to arrange an appointment in a Central London clinic today; patient advised to call the support team number left in notes after five minutes to be slotted into a convenient clinic slot.
    - Further management (e.g., medications, imaging, audiometry, specialist referral) contingent on findings at the in-person assessment.
- Issue 2: Nasal polyps (chronic, intermittent)
  - Assessment:
    - Patient uses an intranasal spray as needed; details/name not recalled.
  - Plan:
    - Continue intranasal spray as previously prescribed PRN; consider updating medication name/dosing during face-to-face visit or medication reconciliation.
- Issue 3: Remote history of labyrinthitis (patient recall only)
  - Assessment:
    - Patient reports a past diagnosis “something like labyrinthitis” but no current symptoms consistent with active inner ear infection beyond intermittent dizziness with tinnitus.
  - Plan:
    - Document history; evaluate vestibular symptoms during in-person assessment; consider ENT or vestibular testing if indicated.

General plan items:
- Urgent same-day face-to-face assessment emphasized by clinician.
- Reassurance provided preliminarily that condition is unlikely to be life-threatening, pending physical examination.
- No medications were prescribed during this teleconsult; further treatment decisions deferred to in-person examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, etc.) not documented.
  - Detailed neurological and cranial nerve examination not available.
  - Audiometry, tympanometry, otoscopic findings, and any imaging results not available.
  - Exact name/dose/route/frequency of intranasal spray and Rennies not documented.
  - Smoking/alcohol/substance use status not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Living situation: patient initially said “live alone” then stated “I live with my partner” — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/dialogue generally clear and intelligible; patient and clinician statements adequately recorded. Some medication names/details were not recalled by patient.
